origins: After abuse, an assault, an accident, a parent’s divorce, or a loved one’s death, many people blame themselves. Children especially assume they caused what happened, because it is less frightening than believing the adults around them were unsafe. Abusers often tell victims it was their fault. Self-blame can also feel like control: if it was my fault, maybe I can prevent it next time.
teaches: Scripture is clear that each person is responsible for his own wrongdoing; the guilt of one is not placed on another. If someone harmed you, the responsibility belongs to the person who did it. God is near to the brokenhearted, and Jesus came to bind up the brokenhearted and set captives free. Where we have truly done wrong, God forgives completely. But where we were wronged, He does not ask us to carry the blame. In Christ, there is no condemnation.
self_statements: If I had been better, it wouldn’t have happened.
I must have done something to cause it.
I should have seen it coming.
errors: Taking responsibility for something another person chose to do.
Judging my past self by what I know now.
Believing I’m to blame because I feel guilty.
Insisting I should have been able to prevent it.
questions: Who actually made the choices that caused harm?
What did I know, and what power did I have, at the time?
Would I blame a child or friend in the same situation?
Did someone tell me it was my fault, and why might they have said that?
Is there anything I truly need to confess, and anything I need to set down?
What does God say about the brokenhearted and about blame?
truth: Something painful happened, and I have carried the blame for it. But responsibility belongs to the person who caused the harm, not to me. I did what I could with what I knew then. God is near to me in my pain, and He does not ask me to carry guilt that isn’t mine.
hw_truths: The guilt of another is not mine to carry.
God is near to the brokenhearted.
I did what I could with what I knew.
Feeling guilty does not make me guilty.
Jesus came to heal the brokenhearted.
In Christ there is no condemnation.
log: Each day, write one self-blaming thought and answer it with a truth from this card.
actions: Draw a circle and divide it among everyone and everything that contributed to what happened. Notice how small, or empty, your slice really is.
Write a short letter to yourself at the age it happened, telling that person what you know now.
Share your story, or part of it, with a counselor, pastor, or trusted friend who will listen without blame.
If what happened was abuse or assault, a counselor trained in trauma can help you heal at a safe pace.
tracker: A time I set down blame
prayer: Lord, I have blamed myself for what happened for so long. Thank You that You are near to the brokenhearted. Help me lay down guilt that is not mine, confess what is, and receive Your healing and peace. Amen.
